title: Pelvic Pain
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} is a sexually active young woman presenting with bilateral lower abdominal/pelvic pain, cervical motion tenderness, adnexal tenderness, purulent cervical discharge, fever, and leukocytosis. Pelvic inflammatory disease is an ascending infection from the lower genital tract — commonly Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae, though polymicrobial. Diagnosis is clinical based on CDC criteria: uterine/adnexal tenderness + cervical motion tenderness (minimum). Complications: tubo-ovarian abscess, infertility, ectopic pregnancy, chronic pelvic pain. Treatment: empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics covering chlamydia, gonorrhea, and anaerobes — ceftriaxone 250mg IM once + doxycycline 100mg PO BID x 14 days + metronidazole 500mg PO BID x 14 days. Partner treatment essential. Screen for other STIs. Admit if severe, TOA, pregnant, or failed outpatient treatment.
chief_complaint: Bilateral pelvic pain, fever, purulent discharge

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Genitalia / Pelvic
stacks.finding: Cervical motion tenderness + adnexal tenderness + purulent discharge = classic PID.

stacks.label: Urinalysis / Urine culture
stacks.finding: Rule out UTI/pyelo — dysuria can overlap.

stacks.label: Chlamydia / Gonorrhea NAAT
stacks.finding: Identify causative organisms. NAAT on cervical swab or urine.

stacks.label: HCG, beta (pregnancy test)
stacks.finding: MUST rule out ectopic pregnancy — can mimic PID.

stacks.label: Pelvic ultrasound
stacks.finding: Rule out tubo-ovarian abscess. Transvaginal preferred.

stacks.label: Doxycycline 100mg PO BID x 14 days
stacks.finding: Covers chlamydia. 14-day course for PID (not 7-day like uncomplicated CT).

stacks.label: Advise patient, sexual partner needs treatment
stacks.finding: Partner treatment essential to prevent reinfection.

physical_exam.abdominal: Bilateral lower quadrant tenderness. No peritoneal signs.
physical_exam.genitourinary: Cervical motion tenderness. Adnexal tenderness (bilateral). Purulent cervical discharge. Uterine tenderness.

decoys.label: Doxycycline x 7 days only
decoys.reason_wrong: PID requires 14-day course, not the 7-day course used for uncomplicated chlamydia. Inadequate duration risks treatment failure and complications.

teach_me_steps.reasoning: Minimum: uterine/adnexal tenderness + cervical motion tenderness. Additional: fever, leukocytosis, purulent discharge, CT/GC positive. Rule out ectopic with HCG.
Empiric coverage: GC (ceftriaxone), CT (doxycycline), anaerobes (metronidazole). 14-day course. Partner treatment essential.

case_summary: PID diagnosed clinically. Cervical motion tenderness + adnexal tenderness + fever + discharge. Ceftriaxone IM + doxycycline x14d + metronidazole x14d. Rule out ectopic. Partner treatment.
